title: Album Cover Rugs: Fitting a Square Cover to a Rectangle
meta_description: Album covers are square, album cover rugs aren't. Compare four rug sizes from $31.85 and see the largest cover each one can hold.
body_html:
An album cover is square, and every album cover rug in our range is a rectangle. The cover can't be wider than the rug's short side. The right size depends on how big you want the cover to look and how much floor you have.

Contents

  1. Why doesn't a square album cover fill a rectangular rug?
  2. What size album cover rug do I need?
  3. A worked example: choosing a size for one room
  4. Is the matching tapestry a better fit for a square cover?
  5. What's underfoot: backing, cushioning and cleaning
  6. Which album rugs should I start with?

Why doesn't a square album cover fill a rectangular rug?

A square has equal sides. A rug doesn't. Each rug size in the Music Lover range is longer than it is wide:

  • 24"x36" is 2:3, so it's 1.5 times as long as it is wide
  • 36"x60" is 3:5, or 1.67 times
  • 48"x72" is 2:3, or 1.5 times
  • 60"x96" is 5:8, or 1.6 times

These ratios are worked out from the listed sizes. They aren't separate figures from the product pages.

A square cover can't be wider than the rug's short side, so some of the rug's length is always left over. On a 24"x36" rug, the largest possible square is 24"x24", and the rest of the 36" length is spare. That's the most the cover could be if it ran edge to edge. Any border or margin in the design makes it smaller.

What a design does with that spare length changes how the whole rug looks, and it varies from design to design. The product photos are where to check. Look at whether the cover runs to the rug's edges or sits inside a border. Then look at what else is printed alongside it, such as a title, a song player bar or a turntable.

How to apply it: decide whether you care more about the cover itself or the rug as a whole. If the cover matters most, size up until the short side is as wide as you want the cover to be.

What to check

  • The rug's short side. That's the widest your cover can be.
  • How much spare length that size leaves.
  • What the product photo shows in the spare space.
  • Whether the photo shows the cover with a border.

What size album cover rug do I need?

Start with the floor, not the picture. Measure the space where the rug will go, then find the largest rug that fits and check how big a cover it can hold. There are 15 designs in the Music Lover Rugs collection, which you can browse by size, and all of them use the same four rug sizes.

Look at the 36"x60" row. It's the longest shape of the four, so its cover takes up the smallest share of the rug.

How to apply it: mark out your rug space on the floor with tape. Then mark a square inside it as wide as the rug's short side. If that square looks too small from where you'll usually see it, try the next size up.

What to check

  • The floor space you measured, length and width.
  • The largest square cover that fits on the rug size you're considering.
  • The price of the design you want in that size, not the lowest price in the table.
  • Whether a door or furniture will cover part of the rug.

A worked example: choosing a size for one room

The figures here are made up to show how the choice works.

Say someone wants an album rug beside a record shelf. The clear floor there is 50" wide and 80" deep. They want the cover to be at least 36" across so it reads from the sofa.

  1. What fits the floor? The 24"x36", 36"x60" and 48"x72" sizes all fit within 50"x80". The 60"x96" is too large on both sides.
  2. What's the cover limit for each? On these three sizes, the largest cover is 24", 36" and 48".
  3. Which sizes meet the 36" goal? The 24"x36" doesn't, so it's ruled out. The 36"x60" meets it exactly, but only if the cover runs edge to edge. The 48"x72" meets it with room to spare.
  4. Check the photo. If the design they like shows the cover inside a border, the cover on a 36"x60" will come out under 36", and that size fails the goal.
  5. Decide. With an edge-to-edge design, the 36"x60" from $64.85 does the job and leaves floor showing on both sides. With a bordered design, the 48"x72" from $101.85 is the size that keeps the cover at 36" or more, and it fills almost the whole width of the space.

Prices are the lowest listed for each size. The design they choose may cost more.

What to check

  • The clear floor space, not the room size.
  • The smallest cover size you'd be happy with, seen from where you usually sit.
  • Whether the design has a border, which shrinks the cover.
  • Prices for the actual design in both sizes.

Is the matching tapestry a better fit for a square cover?

Some designs offer a matching tapestry when you buy the rug, under "Would You Like to Purchase a Matching Tapestry?". Its sizes are much closer to square than any rug size, which matters if the cover is the point.

The 60"x50" option is the closest to square of anything in the range, so it leaves less spare space around a cover than any rug does.

Before comparing these prices with rug prices, pick both a rug size and a tapestry size on the design's page and read the total. That tells you exactly what the tapestry adds to your order. If the page shows a preview of the tapestry, compare it with the rug photo to see whether the cover sits the same way on both.

How to apply it: if you mainly want the cover on show at full size, a tapestry on the wall lets it come closer to its real proportions. The rug can then carry the same design underfoot.

What to check

  • Whether the design you like offers the tapestry option.
  • The wall space for the tapestry size you're considering.
  • The order total with both the rug and the tapestry selected.
  • Whether the tapestry and rug show the cover the same way.

What's underfoot: backing, cushioning and cleaning

The product pages don't all list the same features, so check the page for the design you choose rather than assuming. Across the 15 designs:

  • Non-slip backing. 14 of 15 pages state: "Non-slip point plastic bottom offers reliable floor protection."
  • Cushioning. 9 of 15 pages state: "Constructed with soft short fibers and a high-density sponge for comfort."
  • Cleaning. 6 of 15 pages state: "Easy to clean using a vacuum, broom, damp cloth, or garden hose."
  • Pile height. 5 of 15 pages state: "Low pile height for easy cleaning and maintenance."
  • Edges. 4 of 15 pages state: "Equipped with reinforced serged edges to prevent wear and tear."

These counts come from what each page says. A page that leaves a feature out might mean the rug doesn't have it, or that the description is just shorter. If one of these features matters to you and your design's page doesn't mention it, ask the shop before ordering rather than assuming either way.

How to apply it: match the features to where the rug is going. If it's going by a door that sees mud, look for the cleaning line. If people will sit or stand on it for long periods, look for the cushioning line.

What to check

  • The non-slip backing line on the page for your design.
  • The cushioning line, if comfort matters.
  • The cleaning instructions, if the spot gets dirty.
  • The edge description, if the rug is going somewhere busy.

Which album rugs should I start with?

All 15 pages describe the rugs as personalized: "Serves as a unique and thoughtful personalized gift for music lovers." What you can change, and what you'll need to send, is set out on each design's own page. Some people search for an album receipt rug, a style that lists tracks like a printed receipt. None of the six designs below is named that way, so browse the full collection if that's the look you want.

Here are six designs to start with, with their listed starting prices.

The colour designs are the simplest to compare. The Burgundy Personalized Music Album Rug starts at $33.90.

For a cooler tone, the Gray Personalized Album Cover Rug is also from $33.90.

For a brighter colour, the Orange Personalized Music Album Rug is from $33.90 too.

Two designs start at the lowest listed price. The Custom Music Album Area Rug with a song player design starts at $31.85. Its web address calls it a welcome mat.

The other is the Turntable Personalized Music Rug, also from $31.85.

The Music Studio Album Art Rug starts at $66.90. That's above the lowest price listed for the two smallest sizes, so check which size it refers to before you compare.

What to check

  • The size and price on the design's own page.
  • What you can personalize and what you'll need to provide.
  • Whether the photo shows a border around the cover.
  • Whether the tapestry option is offered for that design.
